Nothing is sweetened with glucose. It is not an added sweetner. I suppose you could go to the hospital and drink a bag of IV D5W or something that is an additive to blood, to get glucose, but you won't find it on the shelf at walmapart.

Majority of fructose is not found by itself, but forming a dimer with glucose, for a final form we are all familiar with: Sucrose. Refined fructose is as artificial as refined glucose (okay, maybe not as much, the proportion of free fructose in several fruits really is higher than that of free glucose, but it's still much less common than sucrose).

You are correct that free glucose is not something we typically would come to have in great quantities as a free sugar in our diets, we'll either eat it as sucrose (with the rest of the fruit/vegetable), or in a polysaccharide form (i.e., starches and the like). The way free glucose hits our pancreas as spikes insulin isn't really something the body should be doing.

Bottom line is, use sucrose for a balance between insulin-spiking and more slowly digested fructose, never on its own, don't abuse it, and better yet, use as much natural product as possible (just eat fruit dammit!). And avoid fructose and glucose syrups!

TIL casinos are making skill-based games as younger people are bored with the standard "luck-based" ones. Gamblers will be able to bet money on things like free throw contests.
Blackjack and poker are games of skill if you know what you are doing.

A lot of the "skill" is predicting what the next card will be. I like games like 5-card draw that involve some player-influence on what cards you have. I hate games like Texas Hold'em where all you're doing is guessing what number is on cards you essentially already have.
My guess would be that this is due to the rise of video games in popular culture.

I don't see any of this happening unless it's in the favor of the house, like having rigged carnival games. I could see the only upside is drawing people in, getting them drunk, and hoping they then waste their money on the luck-based games.

I see it more like the arcades that give you tickets and the tickets purchase ridiculously over priced toys. Even if you sing every free throw you win $3.50 and the game cost $3 is what I am imagining.

From someone who works within the business I can shed some light on how it is expected to work. I'll preface this by saying that I'm working in a state where the regulations for "skill-based gaming" are still in the works, so I haven't heard much information about it yet.

The basic idea though is not that better players will win more often, the idea is that the better players will be put into a higher paytable.

Normally you increase your paytables by betting more per line:

  • If you bet $1 and get 3 cherries in a row, you get $2.
  • If you bet $5 and get 3 cherries in a row, you get $15.

With this new type of game, you're still at mercy of the random number generator, but you can win more money by being a better player:

  • If you bet $1 and get 3 cherries in a row, you get $2.
  • If you bet $1 and get 3 cherries in a row and reach a certain score in candy crush, you get $4
